pathway.title: Bally's Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity is the binding weakness and it is shrinking on a known date. Cash was USD 390,184 thousand and the revolver had USD 195.8 million available at 2026-06-30, together USD 585,984 thousand, and the filing says total revolver availability falls to about USD 319 million from October 2026, which would leave about USD 15.25 million undrawn if read as the commitment limit with the drawn balance unchanged. The company states that without its planned financings it does not project meeting the minimum liquidity requirement of the waiver or the reinstated leverage covenant, so a revolver whose access depends on a test creditors cannot see is the first thing that breaks; pro forma cash after the 2026-07-27 dividend is not established. Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Operations do not fund the business, so every obligation is met from asset sales or borrowing. After cash interest, capital expenditure and capitalised software, adjusted EBITDA leaves USD -128,393 thousand, free cash flow over the last twelve months is USD -532,312 thousand, and capital spending absorbs 38.33% of adjusted EBITDA before rent timing, working capital or licence payments. In the first half of 2026 the group received USD 685,000 thousand from the Twin River sale-leaseback and repaid a net USD 49,087 thousand of debt, which shows that deleveraging so far comes from monetising property into fixed rent rather than from earnings. Basis: calculation B03; calculation B04; calculation B05; calculation B15; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is high on any measure and the parent group carries the worse half. Total debt is 8.79x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and net debt 8.03x, with pro forma net leverage not established, and reported EBITDA is negative over the last twelve months, so no reported-basis leverage can be stated; splitting segment earnings, which is analyst judgement, puts the principal debt of Bally's Corporation at 23.80x its share of adjusted EBITDA against 5.14x at Bally's Intralot. Lenders to the parent group therefore rely on property monetisation and parent-level financing rather than on the Intralot earnings that sit in the consolidated ratio. Basis: calculation B02; calculation B10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Refinancing capacity is weaker for the unsecured notes than for the secured loans, and the real wall is 2029. The disclosed fair value of the 2029 notes is 69.64% of principal and of the 2031 notes 63.00%, against 99.14% for the 2026 term loans, and the term loans mature on 2029-03-01 if the 2029 notes remain outstanding, so USD 1,859,518 thousand, or 37.87% of principal, falls on one refinancing date; 29.14% of principal falls due by the end of 2029. The unsecured notes can only be refinanced on better terms if earnings recover or an equity investor joins, which is why the Bronx financing outcome matters beyond the Bronx. Basis: calculation B08; calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37

Revenue is durable at the regional casinos but margin is not. Casinos & Resorts revenue rose 2.0% and segment Adjusted EBITDAR 3.4% in the second quarter of 2026 and rated visitation rose 4.3%, yet the adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 20.71% in the first half of 2025 to 15.98% in the first half of 2026 and quarterly adjusted EBITDA changed by -4.03% on revenue growth of 20.49%. Triple-net rent takes 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR and the UK gaming tax increase cost about USD 39 million gross in the quarter with close to 65% offset by management action, so fixed claims and regulation, not demand, set the margin. Basis: calculation B11; calculation B12; calculation B13; calculation B14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Financial policy and governance are average at best: a controlling holder with 67.1% of the common stock has received no dividends and no documented fees, but no sponsor equity support is documented while the company buys more Bally's Intralot shares and pursues the evoke offer. Policy therefore adds growth demands to a business that cannot fund its present commitments, and creditor protection rests on documents and lender waivers rather than on sponsor support. Basis: calculation B17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28

In a downside, the first break is the October 2026 revolver step-down and the minimum liquidity test, not an operating collapse. If the Bronx loan and equity do not close, development spending and cash interest continue to draw on a smaller revolver and falling cash; a failed liquidity test ends the waiver and reinstates the leverage covenant, which the company already projects it could not meet, and the filings do not state how the term loans and notes cross-default. The observable triggers are revolver availability, cash, waiver status and the Bronx financing, and the analysis does not state a run-out date because no forecast is supplied. Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; calculation B16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66

runs.text: The strongest credit supports are scale and spread of earnings, asset value and a willing lender group. Revenue is USD 2,957,917 thousand over the last twelve months across US casinos, online gaming and lottery, so no single property or product dominates; the Twin River sale-leaseback shows that real estate can be sold for USD 700.0 million, and lenders have waived rather than enforced. Basis: calculation B13; calculation B17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The weakest points are liquidity, cash conversion and the unfunded development programme. The revolver is the only undrawn source stated for the parent group and it steps down in October 2026, free cash flow is USD -532,312 thousand, rent absorbs 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR, and the Bronx project of USD 4.0 billion has only a non-binding term sheet and a letter of intent. Opportunities that would improve credit quality are a binding Bronx financing, the 2027 Chicago opening and the 2028 Las Vegas stadium, and threats are a failed liquidity test, a further UK tax or regulatory change and a Bally's Intralot acquisition that adds debt. Basis: calculation B04; calculation B07; calculation B11; calculation B16; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The 2025 merger of Bally's Corporation with Standard General's Queen Casino & Entertainment closed on 2025-02-07: Standard General contributed its Queen shares in exchange for new Bally's common stock, public holders not electing to roll received USD 18.25 in cash per share, and Standard General's group ended with 73.8% of the common stock. The Queen merger was accounted for as a transaction between entities under common control, and the company settled Queen's pre-existing debt and issued USD 500.0 million of 11% first-lien notes due 2028 at closing, which it repaid in full on 2025-10-08. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163

On 2025-10-08 the company closed the Bally's Intralot transaction: Bally's Intralot paid USD 1.8 billion of cash and issued new shares for Bally's International Interactive, lifting the company's stake to a controlling 57.9% and creating a 42.1% non-controlling interest, and the company assumed Bally's Intralot debt of USD 1.97 billion at a fair value of USD 1.98 billion. New debt in this group since then comprises EUR 600 million of 6.75% senior secured notes and EUR 300 million of floating-rate notes due 2031, a GBP 400.0 million term loan, a euro term loan and a euro revolver, and on 2026-07-27 Bally's Intralot signed a further GBP 261.8 million of senior secured term facilities. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37

At Bally's Corporation the new debt is the USD 1.1 billion of 2026 term loans signed on 2026-02-11, priced at 750 bp over term SOFR with a 300 bp floor and up to 3.50% payable in kind, which repaid the previous term loan and mature in 2031 unless the 2029 notes remain outstanding on 2029-03-01. The Twin River sale-leaseback to GLPI closed the same day for USD 700.0 million, and the credit agreement amendments of January and May 2026 split the revolver's maturities and raised its margins, while a further amendment dated 2026-07-29 is not described. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 74

Other transactions are the A$200 million investment in The Star from April 2025, now a 37.7% equity stake carried at fair value, the New York licence and land conveyance, and the June 2026 binding offer by Bally's Intralot for evoke plc, whose consideration is not stated in the sources and whose financing is therefore not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 74

fields.value: Bally's Corporation's debt is not covered by its reported earnings: at 2026-06-30 net debt is 8.03x issuer-adjusted last-twelve-month EBITDA, and reported EBITDA is negative over the same twelve months, so repayment depends on asset sales, new financing and the lenders' conditional covenant waiver.

The latest quarterly report states substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern, and the statements carry no adjustment for it. The FY2025 column covers only the Successor period from 2025-02-08, so year-on-year comparisons are not like-for-like.

fields.value: On the issuer-adjusted measure, total debt to EBITDA was 6.70x at FY2024, 9.42x at FY2025 and 8.79x at 2026-06-30, and net debt to EBITDA was 6.35x, 7.75x and 8.03x. Debt rose faster than earnings because Queen joined the group in February 2025 and the debt of Bally's Intralot was consolidated from October 2025, and the FY2025 ratio sets year-end debt against a Successor period shorter than a year; adding the Predecessor period's adjusted EBITDA lowers FY2025 total leverage to 8.96x. On reported EBITDA the ratios are 28.45x at FY2024 and 111.47x at FY2025 and are not calculable at 2026-06-30 because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is negative, so the leverage assessment rests on the issuer's add-backs, none of which is stated as realised or unrealised.

Transaction costs of USD 28,568 thousand and development costs of USD 33,264 thousand in the half-year are added back in every period shown, so creditors should treat adjusted EBITDA as a ceiling on recurring earnings rather than a settled figure.

Last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 444,640 thousand now absorbs most of adjusted EBITDA of USD 512,810 thousand, and the 2026 term loans carry a margin of 750 bp over term SOFR with a floor of 300 bp, so a modest fall in earnings leaves little room above break-even cover.

fields.value: Reported liquidity is thin and shrinking. Cash was USD 390,184 thousand at 2026-06-30 against USD 798,423 thousand at FY2025, and the revolver had USD 195.8 million available against USD 588.1 million. The filing says total revolver availability will fall to about USD 319 million from October 2026; read as the commitment limit, and with USD 303,750 thousand drawn, it would leave about USD 15.25 million undrawn if the drawn balance were unchanged and no letters of credit were outstanding. The as-of date falls after that step-down and no supplied document shows the position since. Restricted cash of USD 97,587 thousand, which includes player deposits, is excluded throughout, and the sources do not split consolidated cash between Bally's Corporation's own group and Bally's Intralot.

fields.value: The consolidated figures combine two obligor groups that are insulated from each other: Bally's Intralot does not guarantee Bally's Corporation's debt and a breach under the Bally's Corporation revolver has no implications under Bally's Intralot's debt documents, so the principal debt of Bally's Intralot of USD 2,011,800 thousand and the USD 2,898,268 thousand of revolver, term loan and note principal at Bally's Corporation sit in separate groups. Splitting last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA by segment, which is analyst judgement and not an issuer measure, Bally's Intralot's segments earn USD 391,035 thousand and carry principal debt of 5.14x that amount, while the Bally's Corporation group earns USD 121,775 thousand after triple-net rent and carries principal debt of 23.80x that amount. The consolidated 8.79x therefore understates the leverage faced by lenders to Bally's Corporation, because it counts Bally's Intralot's earnings, which are shared with its 42.1% minority holders and, as far as the sources show, reach Bally's Corporation only through dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors are exposed to a controlled company whose growth programme has outrun its funded liquidity: no dividends or fee leakage are documented, but no sponsor equity support is either, so sponsor and governance risk is medium and protection rests on documents, not alignment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Half of revenue comes from casinos, most of them leased from one landlord, and 41.14% from Bally's Intralot, a separate obligor group; Chicago, Bronx and Las Vegas commitments, and a controlling holder whose managing partner chairs the board, mean creditor protection rests on the executed documents and lender waivers, not on board independence.

fields.value: One holder controls every creditor-relevant decision, so the board is not an independent check. Standard General beneficially owned 67.1% of the common stock at 2026-02-28, down from 73.8% at the February 2025 merger, the company is a controlled company exempt from independent-board requirements, and Standard General's managing partner is Executive Chairman. Financing, acquisition and distribution decisions therefore reach creditors without a minority check, which makes the legal documents and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement, which restricts distributions and new debt above a leverage of 5.50x on its own definition, the real constraints.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 deals changed what creditors own: Casinos & Resorts fell from 56.75% of Successor-period revenue in FY2025 to 50.44% in the first half of 2026, while Bally's Intralot rose from 34.90% to 41.14%. Bally's Intralot brings lottery contracts and interactive operations in a subsidiary with its own lenders and minority holders, so part of group revenue growth sits behind other claims, and the UK tax increase hit its consumer segment in the second quarter of 2026.

fields.value: Landlord claims sit ahead of lenders in practice and are growing. Triple-net rent takes 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR over the last twelve months, the Twin River sale-leaseback added USD 56.0 million of annual rent in February 2026, and the Chicago ground lease adds 8.5% of every GLPI development advance to rent. After any refinancing, extension or majority amendment of the credit agreement the Chicago ground lease cross-defaults to the two GLPI master leases, so a default under the master leases would then also put the Chicago site and its landlord-funded construction at risk.

Chicago must spend at least USD 1,340.0 million under its host community agreement with about USD 400.0 million remaining and an expected overrun that the filing cannot yet estimate, GLPI advances of up to USD 940.0 million are conditional on the company showing unrestricted access to funds, and the USD 4.0 billion Bronx project has only a non-binding term sheet and a letter of intent behind it after a USD 500.0 million licence fee and USD 115 million of contingent consideration were paid in the first quarter of 2026. If the Bronx financing is not completed, the remaining project obligations would fall on the same liquidity that supports the revolver.

fields.value: Sponsor and company behaviour in the sources is mixed rather than extractive. No cash dividend was paid in either period and the filings state no intention to pay one, and no management or monitoring fee to Standard General appears in the documents read; against that, the company paid USD 416,180 thousand of cash to non-rolling shareholders at USD 18.25 a share in the first quarter of 2025, bought more Bally's Intralot shares for USD 24,359 thousand in the first half of 2026 while liquidity was falling, and entered a total return swap on Bally's Intralot shares of up to EUR 50.0 million in June 2026 ahead of the evoke offer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure quality limits how well creditors can monitor the group. A material weakness over income-tax review remains open at the June 2026 report, disclosure controls were not effective in both the annual and the June report, the annual report was filed under an extension, and the June quarterly report omits market-risk disclosure; the 2026 proxy statement that would carry board composition and compensation is not in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, the evidence supports a medium sponsor and governance risk level. The supported behaviour is a controlling holder presiding over an acquisitive and development-heavy strategy that rests on landlord funding and lender waivers, which matters because it leaves creditors without equity support or board checks and implies refinancing and liquidity risk rather than leakage risk. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends or documented fee extraction and the willingness of lenders to waive; further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit and lease documents, and any sponsor equity commitment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that nothing in the sources shows value leaving the group: no dividend, no related-party fee and no priming transaction appear, Standard General's reported holding is lower at 67.1% than the 73.8% at the merger closing, lenders granted a conditional waiver and amendments instead of enforcing, and GLPI is advancing Chicago construction costs. A binding Bronx loan with third-party equity, a sponsor equity cure or a disclosed absence of fees would move the view toward low risk; a distribution, a related-party transaction funded with debt, a further waiver without deleveraging or an uptier or priming step would move it to high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 merger of Bally's Corporation with Standard General's Queen Casino & Entertainment closed on 2025-02-07: Standard General contributed its Queen shares in exchange for new Bally's common stock, public holders not electing to roll received USD 18.25 in cash per share, and Standard General's group ended with 73.8% of the common stock. The Queen merger was accounted for as a transaction between entities under common control, and the company settled Queen's pre-existing debt and issued USD 500.0 million of 11% first-lien notes due 2028 at closing, which it repaid in full on 2025-10-08.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2025-10-08 the company closed the Bally's Intralot transaction: Bally's Intralot paid USD 1.8 billion of cash and issued new shares for Bally's International Interactive, lifting the company's stake to a controlling 57.9% and creating a 42.1% non-controlling interest, and the company assumed Bally's Intralot debt of USD 1.97 billion at a fair value of USD 1.98 billion. New debt in this group since then comprises EUR 600 million of 6.75% senior secured notes and EUR 300 million of floating-rate notes due 2031, a GBP 400.0 million term loan, a euro term loan and a euro revolver, and on 2026-07-27 Bally's Intralot signed a further GBP 261.8 million of senior secured term facilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At Bally's Corporation the new debt is the USD 1.1 billion of 2026 term loans signed on 2026-02-11, priced at 750 bp over term SOFR with a 300 bp floor and up to 3.50% payable in kind, which repaid the previous term loan and mature in 2031 unless the 2029 notes remain outstanding on 2029-03-01. The Twin River sale-leaseback to GLPI closed the same day for USD 700.0 million, and the credit agreement amendments of January and May 2026 split the revolver's maturities and raised its margins, while a further amendment dated 2026-07-29 is not described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions are the A$200 million investment in The Star from April 2025, now a 37.7% equity stake carried at fair value, the New York licence and land conveyance, and the June 2026 binding offer by Bally's Intralot for evoke plc, whose consideration is not stated in the sources and whose financing is therefore not established.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Bally's Corp (baly), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit_snapshot pathway. It combines the business, financial and governance findings of the earlier modules with the seven supplied filings and releases into one credit view, drivers, monitoring triggers and a downside path. Run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed as a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fundamental credit profile is weak and liquidity-driven: adjusted EBITDA of USD 512,810 thousand covers cash interest only 1.15x, free cash flow is deeply negative, and going-concern doubt means creditors depend on asset monetisation and refinancing rather than internally generated cash.

fields.value: Scale across casinos, online gaming and lottery, a proven ability to sell property for cash and lenders' willingness to waive support the credit; the October 2026 revolver step-down, an unfunded development programme and net debt of USD 4,116,516 thousand, or USD 4,130,416 thousand pro forma for the Bally's Intralot dividend paid on 2026-07-27 with pro forma net leverage not established, weaken it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the binding weakness and it is shrinking on a known date. Cash was USD 390,184 thousand and the revolver had USD 195.8 million available at 2026-06-30, together USD 585,984 thousand, and the filing says total revolver availability falls to about USD 319 million from October 2026, which would leave about USD 15.25 million undrawn if read as the commitment limit with the drawn balance unchanged. The company states that without its planned financings it does not project meeting the minimum liquidity requirement of the waiver or the reinstated leverage covenant, so a revolver whose access depends on a test creditors cannot see is the first thing that breaks; pro forma cash after the 2026-07-27 dividend is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operations do not fund the business, so every obligation is met from asset sales or borrowing. After cash interest, capital expenditure and capitalised software, adjusted EBITDA leaves USD -128,393 thousand, free cash flow over the last twelve months is USD -532,312 thousand, and capital spending absorbs 38.33% of adjusted EBITDA before rent timing, working capital or licence payments. In the first half of 2026 the group received USD 685,000 thousand from the Twin River sale-leaseback and repaid a net USD 49,087 thousand of debt, which shows that deleveraging so far comes from monetising property into fixed rent rather than from earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high on any measure and the parent group carries the worse half. Total debt is 8.79x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and net debt 8.03x, with pro forma net leverage not established, and reported EBITDA is negative over the last twelve months, so no reported-basis leverage can be stated; splitting segment earnings, which is analyst judgement, puts the principal debt of Bally's Corporation at 23.80x its share of adjusted EBITDA against 5.14x at Bally's Intralot. Lenders to the parent group therefore rely on property monetisation and parent-level financing rather than on the Intralot earnings that sit in the consolidated ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing capacity is weaker for the unsecured notes than for the secured loans, and the real wall is 2029. The disclosed fair value of the 2029 notes is 69.64% of principal and of the 2031 notes 63.00%, against 99.14% for the 2026 term loans, and the term loans mature on 2029-03-01 if the 2029 notes remain outstanding, so USD 1,859,518 thousand, or 37.87% of principal, falls on one refinancing date; 29.14% of principal falls due by the end of 2029. The unsecured notes can only be refinanced on better terms if earnings recover or an equity investor joins, which is why the Bronx financing outcome matters beyond the Bronx.

fields.value: Revenue is durable at the regional casinos but margin is not. Casinos & Resorts revenue rose 2.0% and segment Adjusted EBITDAR 3.4% in the second quarter of 2026 and rated visitation rose 4.3%, yet the adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 20.71% in the first half of 2025 to 15.98% in the first half of 2026 and quarterly adjusted EBITDA changed by -4.03% on revenue growth of 20.49%. Triple-net rent takes 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR and the UK gaming tax increase cost about USD 39 million gross in the quarter with close to 65% offset by management action, so fixed claims and regulation, not demand, set the margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are average at best: a controlling holder with 67.1% of the common stock has received no dividends and no documented fees, but no sponsor equity support is documented while the company buys more Bally's Intralot shares and pursues the evoke offer. Policy therefore adds growth demands to a business that cannot fund its present commitments, and creditor protection rests on documents and lender waivers rather than on sponsor support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In a downside, the first break is the October 2026 revolver step-down and the minimum liquidity test, not an operating collapse. If the Bronx loan and equity do not close, development spending and cash interest continue to draw on a smaller revolver and falling cash; a failed liquidity test ends the waiver and reinstates the leverage covenant, which the company already projects it could not meet, and the filings do not state how the term loans and notes cross-default. The observable triggers are revolver availability, cash, waiver status and the Bronx financing, and the analysis does not state a run-out date because no forecast is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak view is that creditors and landlords keep funding the company: lenders conditionally waived the leverage covenant, GLPI is advancing Chicago construction costs, the Twin River sale-leaseback realised USD 700.0 million, Bally's Intralot has signed GBP 261.8 million of new term facilities at 5.14x principal leverage on segment earnings, revenue rose 20.49% in the quarter and casinos are growing slowly but positively. A binding Bronx loan with third-party equity, an extension of the revolver beyond October 2026, an equity sale or a second property monetisation at a similar price would move the view toward average; termination of the waiver, availability near USD 15.25 million, a failure to refinance the 2029 notes or a further fall in quarterly adjusted EBITDA would move it to a distressed view.

fields.value: The strongest credit supports are scale and spread of earnings, asset value and a willing lender group. Revenue is USD 2,957,917 thousand over the last twelve months across US casinos, online gaming and lottery, so no single property or product dominates; the Twin River sale-leaseback shows that real estate can be sold for USD 700.0 million, and lenders have waived rather than enforced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weakest points are liquidity, cash conversion and the unfunded development programme. The revolver is the only undrawn source stated for the parent group and it steps down in October 2026, free cash flow is USD -532,312 thousand, rent absorbs 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR, and the Bronx project of USD 4.0 billion has only a non-binding term sheet and a letter of intent. Opportunities that would improve credit quality are a binding Bronx financing, the 2027 Chicago opening and the 2028 Las Vegas stadium, and threats are a failed liquidity test, a further UK tax or regulatory change and a Bally's Intralot acquisition that adds debt.

Cash-flow visibility is moderate because casino revenue is regional and discretionary while lottery contracts are multi-year, but the group is held by a controlling holder with 67.1% of the common stock and by two separate obligor groups, so visibility at the parent group is lower than the consolidated figures suggest.

fields.value: Revenue visibility is highest at the regional casinos and at lottery contracts and lowest in UK online gaming, where tax rose from 21% to 40% from 2026-04-01 and about USD 39 million of the quarter's earnings was hit before offsets. Operating leverage is high because rent, interest and development spending are fixed, so a small fall in segment earnings removes the cushion after cash interest; capital spending of 38.33% of adjusted EBITDA is only partly discretionary because Chicago is contractually committed.

fields.value: Competitive rivalry is regional, and management named elevated competition in Atlantic City and East Saint Louis as a pressure in the second quarter; entry and substitution risk from online play is not evidenced beyond the company's own strategy of expanding interactive gaming; buyers in lottery are public bodies under long contracts, which supports visibility but needs up-front investment; and the landlord GLPI is the most powerful supplier because rent is fixed and, after a credit agreement refinancing, the Chicago lease cross-defaults to the master leases. Regulation matters to credit through the UK gaming tax increase and through the Rhode Island regulatory agreement, which caps distributions and new debt above a leverage of 5.50x on its own definition; foreign exchange matters because Bally's Intralot's debt is in sterling and euros.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Bally's presents a not fully assessable business profile supported by scale, diversification and asset value, but credit quality is constrained by liquidity, negative free cash flow and fixed landlord claims. Cash-flow durability appears weak because capital spending and cash interest together exceed adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Bronx financing, a revolver extension and the pricing of the 2029 refinancing. The primary downside path is a failed liquidity test after the October 2026 step-down. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the minimum liquidity requirement, a forecast and filings after 2026-08-14. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: liquidity.
